question: Does the 2014 Valenzuela Sewerage System environmental assessment provide fish occurrence evidence, and what waterbody context can safely be retained?

source.titleAsPublished: Environmental Assessment Report: Valenzuela Sewerage System Project
source.publicationDateBasis: Maynilad's official disclosures page search-indexed entry lists this Environmental Assessment Report as published in 2014. The report itself includes a March 21, 2013 public-consultation record; it does not print a separate report issue date in the reviewed pages.
reviewedLocators: Executive summary, printed p. 15 / PDF text around lines 1046-1054: qualitative freshwater statement and project catchment summary.
Chapter 3, printed p. 48 / PDF text around lines 2962-2989: freshwater observation and NMTT/Tullahan hydrology narrative.
Chapter 3, printed p. 50-53 / PDF text around lines 3085-3137: historical project water-quality discussion; not current safety evidence.
source.access: The complete public PDF was text-reviewed through the World Bank document host. No PDF or extracted table/map was retained locally. The official Maynilad disclosure page was located through its indexed result; direct page retrieval timed out during this review.

fishStatements.sourceClaim: The report says the Tullahan River is heavily polluted and that no fish or other freshwater flora and fauna were present, explicitly attributing the statement to observations and interviews.
fishStatements.assessment: This is qualitative, project-era context. The report does not describe a fish-specific sampling design, effort, taxonomic identification, collection date, voucher, or site-level non-detection protocol. It cannot establish fish absence.

fishStatements.sourceClaim: The report says fish and other freshwater flora and fauna were less likely in portions of Tullahan and Meycauayan Rivers based on observation.
fishStatements.assessment: This is a probability statement from observation, not a systematic fish survey or repeatable absence result.

hydrologyContext.reportDescription: The report describes the Valenzuela project catchment in relation to the three named river systems and says streams lead to Manila Bay and are affected by tides. It also calls the Tullahan reach part of the Navotas-Malabon-Tullahan-Tinajeros (NMTT) system and narrates flow from the La Mesa area toward Bangkulasi and Manila Bay.
hydrologyContext.scopeLimit: These are attributed project-report descriptions for hydrology and waterbody discovery. The project catchment, NMTT naming, diagram, and sewerage reach are not independently validated river geometry, municipal boundary, fishing ground, or access evidence.

separateLaterSurvey.finding: The separate 2024 NMT study reports a three-site fish survey; its Site 3 is described as downstream leading to Tullahan River, but the printed DMS coordinate has 60 seconds and remains malformed. The source rows therefore do not establish a precise feature or capture-point match to the 2014 assessment's qualitative statement.
separateLaterSurvey.interpretation: Keep the historical qualitative assessment and later river-system survey distinct. Neither source supports a present-day fish-presence/absence conclusion for a canonical Tullahan reach.

findings.coordinateGuard: The assessment prints coordinates for the proposed sewerage-treatment-plant property. That infrastructure coordinate is not a fish or river-sampling location and was not used as occurrence geometry.

rights.itemSpecificReuseTerms: No item-specific license or permission to reproduce the report, figures, maps, or underlying observations was verified. Public availability on World Bank and Maynilad disclosure pages is not treated as an open reuse license.
rights.disposition: Use attributed factual scope notes for internal research only. Do not redistribute report prose, figures, maps, tables, or derivative geometry without a separate rights review.

decision.disposition: Retain as historical hydrology and waterbody-scope context only. Do not interpret its observation/interview-based no-fish statement as biological absence or current river condition.

nextActions: Cross-reference Tullahan, Polo, and Meycauayan names against independent waterbody inventories and river-basin datasets without treating this project catchment as a channel boundary.
Keep the 2024 NMT survey's malformed Site 3 coordinate unresolved unless an authoritative correction or original field record becomes available.
Continue NCR freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland source discovery; retain no-fish narratives as time- and method-limited context.

sources.supports: The Valenzuela Sewerage System Environmental Assessment Report, including the project-era observation/interview-based fish statement, freshwater discussion, named river systems, and hydrology narrative.
Maynilad's official indexed disclosure entry identifies the Valenzuela Sewerage System Environmental Assessment Report as published in 2014.
Separate 2024 Navotas-Malabon-Tullahan fish survey review; Site 3's Tullahan-related description and malformed coordinate remain unresolved.
